title: Tooling: pack cyclic routing states with identical exhaustive receipts
body:
The historical cyclic routing checker stores more than half a million nested scalar/routing states. This replaces those state keys with an injective, order-preserving integer encoding, reducing verification time and Python allocation peaks while retaining every original exhaustive-search receipt. **Tooling improvement; no new κ or negative result.**

## Contributor

**4RchYMing** ([GitHub](https://github.com/4RchYMing), authenticated account ID 275918740). Git author: `4RchYMing <275918740+4RchYMing@users.noreply.github.com>`, explicitly specified by the contributor. The predecessor's authorship and notices remain intact.

## AI Assistance

Prepared with **substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** for implementation, mathematical reasoning, independent test implementation, experiments, documentation, and delivery. No independent human peer review is claimed.

## Base Commit

`66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60` is the original implementation and benchmark baseline. Upstream subsequently advanced to `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`; all 19 relevant original checker/certificate, pinned dependency, test-runner and CI input files there are byte-identical. The compatibility receipt is retained in `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json`. OS-cryptographic assignment seed **87**, verification-engineering track. Three candidates, measurements, the local claim, and overlap review are recorded in `research/cyclic-routing-performance/SELECTION.json`. There is no pinned coordination issue.

## Research Scope

Only `audit_cyclic_topology.routing_state_search`: two-port XOR words on 2, 3, or 4 arbitrary-input roles, with the existing depth cap of seven. Preserve scalar/routing joint-state distinctions, full-routing saturation pruning, stopping rules, terminal tests, every frontier digest, and all eight cyclic seed controls. Selected-frontier records, `upstream/`, and the contributor list are unchanged. The #741 frontier selected by newer upstream commits is outside this contribution.

## Method

Place each scalar row in a separate fixed-width integer lane and the complete routing bit set in the low bits. The encoding is injective and preserves the original tuple ordering. XOR updates affect only the target lane; the routing extension remains unchanged. Decode sorted keys to preserve the exact original hash input. The README proves these invariants and explains why the permutation lookup agrees with the old predicate on reachable invertible matrices.

Only the historical certificate's changed checker-source binding is regenerated. Benchmark processes load the original implementation from its pinned Git object and compare the **entire** certificate after restoring that one binding. Source dependencies and the original certificate are hash-pinned.

## Results

- **529,066 four-role states**, all frontier digests, terminal counts, saturation counts, and complete historical certificate fields are preserved.
- Final seven alternating fresh-process pairs on Windows 10 / CPython 3.12.14: complete-process median **3.788324 s → 2.680431 s**, **1.413× faster / 29.24% less elapsed time**. The earlier seven-pair run is retained too: **1.368×**. All 80 receipts across five benchmark series, including the separate memory runs, agree.
- Separately traced Python allocation peak: **131,099,209 → 80,510,849 bytes**, **38.59% lower**. This is not RSS; tracing is disabled in timing runs.
- **Full independent coverage:** the dense-F2/literal-permutation-set oracle checks every cap 0–7 for all three widths, including all 529,066 four-role states. Every receipt field agrees. A scalar-only merge control loses coverage despite retaining the same negative Boolean and is detected.
- **14 tests pass on each of CPython 3.11.16, 3.13.15 and 3.14.7**, plus all 14 under 3.14.7 `-O` (56 successful test executions). `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json` retains command output and source hashes.
- Minimal offline replays in a path with spaces pass. Modified dependencies, reused output paths, and invalid parameters are rejected. Selected-record/source-inventory and staged whitespace checks pass. `VALIDATION.txt` retains command output.

Additional same-host, same-input pairs on the CI interpreter versions show that the speedup varies by interpreter:

| CPython | Original process median | Packed process median | Speedup | Python allocation peak reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3.11.16 | 3.436026 s | 2.553110 s | 1.346x | 38.59% |
| 3.13.15 | 3.628811 s | 2.902232 s | 1.250x | 38.61% |
| 3.14.7 | 3.842965 s | 3.198651 s | 1.201x | 42.42% |

Each row uses seven alternating fresh-process pairs and separate memory runs. All samples, including the more variable 3.14 timings, are retained. These are within-version comparisons; **1.413x is not a universal guarantee**.

## Reproduction

Python 3.11+ standard library and Git; use a full clone containing the base commit and a fresh output path:

```sh
python3 -B research/cyclic-routing-performance/benchmark.py --pairs 7 --out routing-benchmark.json
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_cyclic_routing_packed.py -v
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_finite_bit_contract.py -v
```

Expected: `PASS_IDENTICAL_COMPLETE_ROUTING_RECEIPTS`; five and nine tests pass. `SOURCE.json`, `RESULT.json`, `INITIAL-RESULT.json`, `RESULT-python311.json`, `RESULT-python313.json`, `RESULT-python314.json`, `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json`, and `EXPLORATION.json` retain pins, exact dependency versions, all measurements, and exploratory evidence. Repeat the commands under each Python interpreter with fresh benchmark output paths; add `-O` before `-m` to reproduce the optimized-mode tests. The README gives the argument and review map.

## Limitations

This measures one historical verifier, not selected-supplier replay or multiplication runtime. OS caches were not flushed; absolute timings vary. There is one separately traced memory run per mode in each benchmark series. The four-role frontier remains unclosed; no claim extends beyond depth seven. The independent implementation shares the documented joint-state reduction and saturation rule; it does not independently prove those reductions. This is not a Lean formalization or a new multiplication theorem, and all inherited transfer/physical/compiler/precision/tape/analytic assumptions remain.

Full `make verify`, the selected cold replay, Lean, and remote Linux CI were not run locally. This Windows environment lacks `make` and a C++ compiler. The local version matrix ran on Windows. Upstream Actions returned `action_required`, requiring maintainer approval; Linux CI and maintainer review are separate from this local evidence.

## Prior Work

Douglas R. Colkitt's original checker, certificate, and `docs/research/cyclic-topology-audit.md` provide the routing obstruction and finite-state reduction (historical source commit `d55bcd62ceb8f322bcf311a5a66e94c3ac7724f0`). Original notices and Apache-2.0 licensing remain.

eumemic's pending [#154](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/154) profiles other verifier hotspots; Victor Li's pending [#756](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/756) optimizes the distinct balanced-Fano search. Neither supplies code here. The original overlap refresh covered 614 open PRs through #795 and fresh arrivals through #799. The follow-up checked the 100 latest open PRs through #820; only this PR matched the cyclic-routing optimization scope. Earlier original-hash inventories and frozen supplier copies are preserved as historical provenance.
